cards.explanation: The answer is sacrifices for their gods, friends. The daughters of Moab invited the men to the sacrifices for their gods (Numbers 25:2). An invitation can sound small, but look where this one led. The people ate and bowed down to those gods, and that's where the chapter turns heavier.

The answer is False. The text says, "And the people ate and bowed down to these gods." (Numbers 25:2). They didn't just watch, friends. They took part, and verse 3 says Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.

The answer is that His anger burns against them, friends. The text says, "…the anger of the LORD burned against them." (Numbers 25:3). Worshiping a false god was a serious matter. This is what the LORD's response looks like, and everything after it in the chapter follows from it.

The answer is so His fierce anger may turn away from Israel. That's the reason the LORD gives, friends. He says it plainly: "…so that His fierce anger may turn away from Israel." (Numbers 25:4). It's a heavy command, and I think it's one to read slowly. The text gives us the reason, and we can stay right there with it.

The answer is judges. Moses told "…the judges of Israel…" and gave them the order: "Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor." (Numbers 25:5). Each judge is handed the job for his own men, friends. I think that's a heavy thing to be asked to carry.

The answer is True, friends. The text says this happened "…in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting." (Numbers 25:6). So the whole community was already weeping when this happened. I think that tells us how heavy the moment was.

The answer is that the plague against them is halted, bakers. Verse 8 says, "So the plague against the Israelites was halted…" (Numbers 25:8). It happens right after Phinehas acts. Verse 9 then tells us the cost of the plague, and it's a heavy number.

The answer is 24 thousand, friends. Verse 9 says, "…those who died in the plague numbered 24,000." (Numbers 25:9). This is one of the heaviest parts of the chapter. It's a number we should read slowly and quietly.

The answer is that he was zealous for the LORD's sake, bakers. The LORD says Phinehas "…was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal." (Numbers 25:11). Zealous means burning with devotion. The LORD says it was "…for My sake…" so He is the one Phinehas's zeal was for. The LORD even uses the same word, zeal, for Himself in that verse.

The answer is that the LORD is granting him His covenant of peace, friends. The LORD says, "Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace." (Numbers 25:12). It's a gift from the LORD to Phinehas. I think it's a good word to land on after such a heavy chapter.

The answer is True, bakers. The LORD says, "It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants…" (Numbers 25:13). Permanent is a strong word. The gift reaches past Phinehas to his descendants too.

The answer is that he made atonement for them, friends. The LORD says Phinehas "…was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites." (Numbers 25:13). Atonement is the word for making things right with God. In the same speech, the LORD says Phinehas turned His wrath away from the Israelites (Numbers 25:11). Both of those were done for the people.

The answer is Zur, bakers. Verse 15 says Cozbi was "…the daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family." (Numbers 25:15). So Zur was a leader among the Midianites. Cozbi gets her name here, and I think that matters.

The answer is that they deceived Israel in the matter of Peor, friends. The LORD says, "For they assailed you deceitfully when they seduced you in the matter of Peor…" (Numbers 25:18). That's the reason He gives for the order. It ties back to the very beginning of the chapter.
